rounds.response:
Proposed cross‑jurisdiction memo structure (headings + what each will cover): 1) Executive summary — launch decision yardstick, top 3 derailers and recommended minimum mitigations; 2) Product description & complexity assessment — plain‑English payoff, key complexity drivers, threshold where supervisor may demand simpler packaging or refuse retail distribution; 3) Digital‑asset exposure — exact nature/route of exposure (direct token vs pooled/derivative), valuation/custody/counterparty risks, likely Market A legal characterisation issues; 4) Distribution & cross‑border controls — booking models, platform/IFA flows, geo‑gating, required notifications/filings and distributor contractual obligations; 5) Suitability, disclosures & complaints handling — target client gates, required disclosure menu (risk summary, examples, costs), mandatory suitability scripts and remediation approach for complaints; 6) Regulatory risk matrix & engagement plan — per‑market likelihood/severity and proposed short responses; 7) Operational/legal mitigations & monitoring — enforceable controls, audit trails, ongoing limits and escalation triggers. 
Regulator‑facing Q&A framing (high level): Complexity — lead with a single‑page plain‑language product summary and standardized numeric example, commit to retail eligibility gates and shortened “key risks” box (lean on proportionality where allowed, but be candid that complexity remains and explain mitigations); Digital‑asset exposure — state the exposure model calmly, disclose valuation/custody regime and third‑party oversight, avoid definitive legal characterisation unless counsel supports it (we can lean on tech‑neutral framing where credible, but flag legal uncertainty and controls to mitigate it); Cross‑border distribution — explain booking/marketing flows, contractual obligations on platforms, geo‑blocking proof and real‑time monitoring, and offer a narrow notification or enhanced distributor attestations rather than broad local filings where permitted. 
Material risks currently under‑weighted in marketing/controls: prominence/transparency of the digital‑asset element in client materials, robustness/technical evidence of geo‑blocking/platform gating for Market A, and a documented faster complaint/escalation path tied to the uploaded complaints extract. 
Next step: I will draft the full memo + regulator Q&A with proposed disclosure language and a short per‑market risk matrix for review within 12–18 hours; confirm whether you want us to prepare a brief pre‑submission note for Market A (written only) or explicitly avoid pre‑submission engagement.
